dedupe_keys.name: urban network analysis una toolbox for arcgis mit city form lab

description: The Urban Network Analysis toolbox from MIT's City Form Lab computes graph measures on spatial networks in ArcGIS: reach, gravity, betweenness, closeness and straightness, plus redundancy tools for the redundancy index, redundant paths and wayfinding index. It handles both geometry and topology, with metric or topological (turn) distances as impedance; adds buildings as a third network element and the unit of analysis, so neighbouring buildings on one street can score differently; and lets buildings be weighted by volume, population or importance. It is aimed at urban designers, architects, planners, geographers and spatial analysts, scales from dense urban areas to regional networks, and is documented by Sevtsuk and Mekonnen (2012) and later papers, including a version for Rhinoceros 3D. Coverage: generic. Access: free download of version 1.01 with help and a forum. Licence: not stated on the page. Caveats: needs ArcGIS 10 with the Network Analyst extension. Simulation uses: accessibility and pedestrian flow potential for public space and facility planning. Related records: cityseer, depthmapX and momepy.
